en.name: Baby food, vegetables
en.summary: Unopened vegetable purée should be discarded after the use-by date on the jar or pouch. Once opened, it keeps 2 days in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below — and only if it has never been fed from directly with a used spoon.
en.pantry: An unopened jar or pouch is commercially processed and shelf-stable to its use-by date; after that date, discard it rather than judging it by eye. No general pantry figure is given here, because the date on the container is the manufacturer's own statement about their own product. Keep it cool and dark, and check every jar before opening: if the vacuum button clicks when pressed, or a pouch is swollen, leaking or damaged, it goes in the bin unopened.
en.fridge: 2 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below once opened, covered. Vegetable purées are low-acid, which is why they get a shorter window than fruit — there is no acidity holding bacteria back. The rule that matters more than the number is the spoon: never feed straight from the jar or pouch with a spoon that has been in the baby's mouth, because saliva carries bacteria and enzymes into the remainder, which then cannot be kept at all. Spoon a portion into a bowl, feed from the bowl, and throw away what is left in the bowl after the feed.
en.freezer: Commercial jars separate when frozen and thawed, which is unappetising rather than unsafe. Freezing your own vegetable purées in an ice cube tray and bagging the cubes once solid works well: freeze them the day you make them and label the bag with the date. Never refreeze a portion that has been thawed, warmed or fed from.
en.thawing: Thaw a frozen home-made portion in the fridge, never on the counter, and warm it once. Stir thoroughly and test on your wrist, because warmed purée forms hot spots that will scald a baby's mouth.
spoilage: A vacuum button that clicks when pressed — discard the jar without opening it.
A swollen or leaking pouch, or any hissing or spurting when opened.
A sour or off smell, or a purée that has darkened noticeably.
Mould around the rim, under the lid or at the spout.
tips: Spoon a portion into a bowl; never feed from the container with a used spoon.
Write the date and time on the jar when you open it.
Vegetable purées are low-acid, so give them the shortest window rather than the benefit of the doubt.
Never give honey to a baby under one year old — it can carry the spores that cause infant botulism.

faq.q: How long does opened baby vegetable purée keep?
faq.a: 2 days in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, covered, and only if it has never been fed from directly.

faq.q: Why do vegetables keep less well than fruit once opened?
faq.a: Vegetable purées are low-acid, so there is nothing holding bacteria back. Fruit purées are acidic and get a slightly longer window.

faq.q: Can you keep what is left after feeding?
faq.a: No. Once a used spoon has been in it, saliva has carried bacteria into the food and the remainder must be thrown away.

zh.name: 嬰兒蔬菜泥
zh.summary: 未開封的嬰兒蔬菜泥，過了罐子或軟袋上的有效日期就該丟掉。開封後放 4 °C 以下冷藏可放 2 天——而且前提是從來沒有用餵過的湯匙直接從裡面挖。
zh.pantry: 未開封的玻璃罐或軟袋經過商業加工，在有效日期之前屬於常溫商品；過了日期就丟，不要用眼睛判斷。這裡不給通用的常溫數字，因為容器上的日期就是製造商對自家產品的說法。請放陰涼避光處，而且每一罐開封前都要檢查：真空鈕按下去會響、軟袋鼓脹滲漏破損的，不要打開，直接丟掉。
zh.fridge: 開封後蓋好放 4 °C 以下 2 天。蔬菜泥屬於低酸食品，這就是它的期限比水果泥短的原因——沒有酸度可以壓住細菌。比數字更重要的是湯匙這條規則：絕對不要用進過寶寶嘴巴的湯匙，直接從罐子或軟袋裡餵，因為口水會把細菌和酵素帶進剩下的部分，那一份就完全不能再留。請舀一份到碗裡、從碗裡餵，餵完碗裡剩下的丟掉。
zh.freezer: 市售罐裝冷凍再解凍會分離，那是難吃而不是不安全。自己打的菜泥很適合用製冰盒冷凍、凍硬後裝袋：打好的當天就凍，袋上貼好日期。已經解凍、加熱或餵過的那一份，絕對不要再冷凍。
zh.thawing: 自製的冷凍份量請放冷藏解凍，絕對不要放檯面，而且只加熱一次。餵之前確實攪拌並滴在手腕內側試溫，因為加熱過的泥會有局部過燙的熱點，會燙傷寶寶的嘴。
spoilage: 真空鈕按下去會響——不要打開，整罐丟掉。
軟袋鼓脹或滲漏，或開封時嘶嘶作響、噴出來。
聞起來發酸或有異味，或泥的顏色明顯變深。
瓶口、蓋子內側或吸嘴處出現霉。
tips: 舀一份到碗裡；絕對不要用餵過的湯匙就著容器餵。
開封時在罐子上寫下日期和時間。
蔬菜泥是低酸食品，請給它最短的期限，不要往寬鬆的方向想。
未滿一歲的寶寶絕對不能吃蜂蜜——它可能帶有引起嬰兒肉毒桿菌中毒的孢子。

faq.q: 開封的嬰兒蔬菜泥可以放多久？
faq.a: 蓋好放 4 °C 以下冷藏 2 天，而且前提是從來沒有直接從裡面餵過。

faq.q: 為什麼蔬菜泥開封後比水果泥更不耐放？
faq.a: 蔬菜泥是低酸食品，沒有酸度可以壓住細菌。水果泥偏酸，期限稍微長一點。
不行。只要餵過的湯匙進去過，口水就已經把細菌帶進食物裡，剩下的必須丟掉。
